name: Lungfish
label: Dischord
lede: A tattoo artist who read poems over tape loops started a band that held one riff until it turned into weather. Lungfish made eleven albums for Dischord, most with Ian MacKaye producing, and sounded like nobody else on the label.

eras.title: Reading poems to tape loops
eras.text: Lungfish didn't start as a rock band. Daniel Higgs read poetry in Baltimore over friends' sound collages, and the band grew out of that slowly, forty miles up the road from the D.C. scene that would release everything they made.

years.src: The Quietus · Dischord · Baltimore Entertainment Archive
years.h: A band that lasts three or four shows leaves Lungfish behind
years.p: [[Daniel Higgs|6dd4abcc-0321-4ac0-b3bf-0a9422c450d9]] and [[Asa Osborne|4314be59-8f9c-453b-a2bc-7ca086d36a10]] had played together in Reptile House, a Baltimore band that managed three or four shows. Wikipedia dates Lungfish to 1987; most sources start the clock in 1988.
years.xp: The Quietus and Wikipedia put the start at 1987, with Higgs coming out of Reptile House. Dischord and the Baltimore Entertainment Archive say 1988, and the Archive lists Reptile House drummer Gary Breezee in the first Lungfish line-up.

years.h: Tape loops and poems grow a rhythm section
years.p: The loops under Higgs' poems turn into guitar, bass and drums: Osborne, bassist [[John Chriest|4c8b5547-f186-42fd-bc35-47cb13d3030c]] and drummer [[Mitchell Feldstein|769a0231-546e-43e8-bcdd-3a2e13499a37]], Osborne's bandmate from Per Capita.
years.xp: The Baltimore Entertainment Archive lists Reptile House's Gary Breezee as Lungfish's first drummer, with Mitchell Feldstein coming in after him.

years.h: One song on a sampler is Lungfish's first release
years.p: Return Descender turns up on the Merkin Seedy Sampler compilation in 1989, a year before the band's first album.

years.h: Simple Machines wants the debut tape, and Dischord backs the release
years.p: Lungfish record Necklace of Heads, then Daniel Higgs moves to San Francisco. Simple Machines, the D.C. label, puts it out with Dischord's backing.
years.xp:
Joab Jackson's 1993 profile has the order: Simple Machines wanted the tape, Dischord backed a shared release, and Dischord then signed the band for what came next. Wikipedia says it wasn't a straight Dischord release.

Dischord later paired it with Talking Songs for Walking on a single CD, Dischord No. 66.

eras.title: A six-week tour, then Dischord
eras.text: After a six-week U.S. tour, Dischord signed Lungfish, and the band worked fast and cheap: three albums in six studio days total, most made in Arlington, Virginia. Everybody kept a day job. The records got stranger and more hypnotic.

years.cap: Lungfish on stage at The Library, Denton, Texas, June 15, 1991
years.h: Six weeks on the road, and Dischord wants another record
years.p: Lungfish finish a six-week U.S. tour behind Necklace of Heads, and Dischord Records signs them to make more albums. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] goes on to produce most of what they record.
years.xp: Joab Jackson's 1993 profile gives the sequence: debut tape, six weeks on the road, then Dischord asking them back into a studio. Everyone kept the day job.

years.h: Talking Songs for Walking arrives as Dischord No. 65
years.p: Lungfish's first full Dischord album runs on repetition, not solos. Bassist John Chriest names [[Miles Davis|561d854a-6a28-4aa7-8c99-323e6ce46c2a]] and [[John Coltrane|b625448e-bf4a-41c3-a421-72ad46cdb831]] as the model: everybody listening, nobody showing off.
years.xp: Bandcamp Daily, reviewing it with Necklace of Heads, calls the pair relatively accessible in sound and says they barely hint at the experimenting to come. It singles out Put Your Hand in My Hand and Descender.

years.big: "If more bands did that they would have less stress."
q: If more bands did that they would have less stress
years.h: Six studio days cover all three albums
years.p: Drummer Mitchell Feldstein tells Joab Jackson in 1993 that Lungfish have recorded every album so far in six days total. Rainbows from Atoms is the third, Dischord No. 78.
years.xp: Ian MacKaye's brother Alec appears on You Might Ask Me Why, per Bandcamp Daily, which also points to Open House, Mother Made Me and Creation Story.

years.h: Nobody in Lungfish quits the day job
years.p: In 1993 bassist John Chriest works at the Golden Temple health food store, drummer Mitchell Feldstein is a licensed social worker, guitarist Asa Osborne moves art, and singer Daniel Higgs tattoos.

years.h: Chriest leaves, and Nathan Bell picks up the bass
years.p: After Rainbows from Atoms, bass passes from John Chriest to [[Nathan Bell|b00a5223-e0c4-4ffd-90c2-d610b396af53]], who holds it through the 1990s. Bell later joins LandSpeedRecord.

years.cap: Lungfish outside a house in Bloomington, Indiana, after their van broke down, 1994
years.h: Nathan Bell's first Lungfish album, Pass and Stow
years.p: Dischord No. 92 is the fourth album and the first after John Chriest's exit.

eras.title: An album a year
eras.text: Lungfish kept a rhythm as steady as their riffs, a record almost every year, each one another turn of the same slow wheel. Dischord's own description is a continuous quasi-musical pulse that reached its climax at semi-monthly public performances.

years.h: Sound in Time opens a run of four albums in four years
years.p: Dischord No. 97 is Lungfish's fifth album, two years after Pass and Stow.

years.h: Live at Lounge Ax, Chicago, 1996
Indivisible keeps the volume down
years.p: Dischord No. 106, a year after Sound in Time. Bandcamp Daily calls it the band's quietest and least-appreciated album, and one of their finest.

yt: Full set, Teamsters Hall, Baltimore, May 12, 1998
years.h: Lungfish alternate words and instrumentals on Artificial Horizon
years.p: Dischord No. 115 is Lungfish's seventh album, split between instrumental and vocal tracks.
years.xp:
Amy Pickering appears on Pray for the Living; Bandcamp Daily also picks out Ann the Word and Shed the World.

The clip is a full set from the Teamsters Hall in Baltimore on May 12, 1998.

years.h: Live at the Black Cat, March 28, 1998
yt: Live at the Black Cat, March 28, 1998

years.h: The Unanimous Hour lands while the next session is underway
years.p: Dischord No. 117 is the eighth album, which Bandcamp Daily hears as fuller-sounding and more energetic. The band is already recording the session later released as A.C.R. 1999.

years.h: Six shelved songs come back at Inner Ear
years.p: Lungfish redo six of the ten songs from the 1999 A.C.R. session with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] at Inner Ear Studios. Necrophones is Dischord No. 119; the other four stay unreleased until 2012.
years.xp: Bandcamp Daily's picks from it: Blue Sky, Hanging Bird, The Words and All Day and All Night Long.

eras.title: Then the pulse stops
eras.text: With Sean Meadows, a bassist from Chattanooga, Lungfish made two last albums, including Love Is Love, which Bandcamp Daily calls perhaps their most magnificent release. Then they stopped, with nothing that looked like an ending.

years.cap: Daniel Higgs at the mic, Fireside Bowl, Chicago, 2003
years.h: Sean Meadows takes the bass from Nathan Bell
years.p: [[Sean Meadows|22a4c5b1-5090-4ec2-b549-95aa5b217fb9]], from Chattanooga, Tennessee, joins for the final line-up: Daniel Higgs, Asa Osborne, Meadows and Mitchell Feldstein.

years.h: Love Is Love gets a "magnificent" from Bandcamp Daily
years.p: Dischord No. 137, Sean Meadows' first album on bass. Bandcamp Daily calls it "perhaps their most magnificent release."
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily points to the title track, Lay Yourself Aside and Hear the Children Sing.

The video is a full Chicago set that the uploader dates to December 6, 2003, at the Fireside Bowl.

years.cap: Lungfish at O-Nest, Shibuya, Tokyo, April 25, 2004
years.h: Lungfish go to California for Feral Hymns
years.p: Dischord No. 147 is the last album and the first made far from home, with [[Tim Green|19b6bda7-fbb1-4a45-a3c7-687114167e8c]] producing.
years.xp: Daniel Higgs told The Quietus: "the final Lungfish record is the only one that really sounds like the band to me." He had assumed recording would always disappoint him sonically, and this one changed that.

years.big: "With those two records the quest was over."
q: With those two records the quest was over.
years.h: Lungfish stop, and nobody says so
years.p: Dischord's own page calls the band "quasi, if not entirely, defunct." Daniel Higgs, to The Quietus, on the last two albums.
years.xp:
Higgs was blunt about band life: "Good music comes out of being in a band, but it comes out of strife, and that gets old." After Feral Hymns he went solo, releasing records on Northern Liberties, Thrill Jockey and Holy Mountain and showing his visual art internationally. "I could just go wandering on my own, through myself," he said.

Asa Osborne started recording alone as The Zomes. Wikipedia puts Lungfish's active years at 1988 to 2006; Dischord's page says about 2005.

eras.title: Higgs goes solo, the vault opens
eras.text: Daniel Higgs became a cult solo artist and Asa Osborne built The Zomes, while Dischord kept the catalog alive with vinyl reissues, a radio documentary and one lost album, A.C.R. 1999, pulled from the vault.

years.h: Higgs goes solo with Ancestral Songs
years.p: The Lungfish singer's first solo record comes a year after Feral Hymns. Metempsychotic Melodies follows in 2007.

yt: Radio Waves for Viewing, the public radio documentary
years.h: Public radio gets Higgs on tape, which Dischord calls very rare
years.p: Dischord points fans to a Publicradio.net documentary on Lungfish with a Daniel Higgs interview. The label notes the band is inactive and Higgs is booking solo dates in the UK.

years.h: Love Is Love gets pressed as an LP
years.p: Dischord's November news post announces the vinyl edition alongside Daniel Higgs' newest CD.

years.h: After 13 years on the shelf, A.C.R. 1999
years.p: Dischord releases ten songs Lungfish recorded with Craig Bowen at A.C.R. Studios in Baltimore in 1999 and then shelved. It's Dischord No. 174.
years.xp:
The line-up was Daniel Higgs, Asa Osborne, Nathan Bell and Mitchell Feldstein. Six of the songs were re-recorded for Necrophones in 2000; the other four had never been released in any version.

Dischord priced it at $18 on metallic silver vinyl and $10 on CD.

years.h: Higgs and Fumie Ishii form Fountainsun
years.p: Higgs also works with the Swedish band [[The Skull Defekts|c4482003-7968-4b29-87ea-bb86c8ffda05]] around the same time.

years.h: Dischord puts Sound in Time back on vinyl
years.p: Lungfish's 1996 album returns to LP on June 24.

eras.title: Still pressing
eras.text: Twenty years after their last recording, Dischord is still pressing Lungfish records.

years.h: Feral Hymns gets a blue vinyl repress
years.p: Twenty years after the last Lungfish recording, Dischord presses the final album again, this time on blue vinyl.
